text:
elaine: noticed a p99 jump on the slo route right after the canary deploy at ~12:34pm. p95 looks fine, but p99 went from ~190ms -> ~820ms. posting traces and a quick summary.
chris: saw the traces. small fraction (~0.2-0.5%) of requests show heavy tail. common pattern: very long user prefix + function-calling recursion -> extra token churn.
samir: KV cache metrics for those traces are terrible — miss rate ~65% on affected traces vs 10-12% baseline. looks like prefix keys aren't matching due to frequent small regenerations.
alex: kernel chooser picked the 'fused-matmul-v2' path for a lot of these, which favors throughput for medium seqs. but for very long prefixes that interact with KV cache we should prefer the 'smallseq-kv-optimized' kernel. heuristic misfire.
elaine: also saw microbatch growth in the same timeframe — queueing pushed effective microbatch to 20-24 for slo traffic which amplified latency when the kernel hot path switched.
chris: attached a short perf output from one trace (trimmed):
```
trace_id: g9f2-71
stage: decode
kernel: fused-matmul-v2
kv_miss_rate: 0.65
microbatch_size: 22
latency_ms: 812
cpu_wait_ms: 48
kernel_warmup_ms: 42
```
samir: paste of the token-level progression from the trace — you can see repeated tool_call/assistant cycles that re-emit prefixes and confuse the kv-tagging: 
```
user: <long prompt, ~9k tokens>
assistant: tool_call -> external_api (returns small structured data)
assistant: regeneration (adds 30 tokens)
assistant: tool_call -> external_api (again)
... loop x3
```
alex: that re-entrancy pattern means the runtime keeps generating slightly different tokenizations for the same logical prefix, so cached key lookups miss and we pay full KV loads + kernel switch cost.
elaine: quick mitigation proposal: 1) cap microbatch for slo-tier to 12, 2) add a short-circuit in kernel chooser to prefer smallseq-kv-optimized when prefix_token_count > 2048 or kv_miss_rate_est > 0.2, 3) add logging for kernel decisions and kv-key fingerprints.
chris: I'll open a small PR for the logging + experiment flag for microbatch cap. also adding an A/B to force the alternate kernel on the canary.
samir: on the KV side I can push a conservative change to make prefix-key normalization deterministic across tiny regen diffs (strip trailing assistant tokens and whitespace before hashing). should drop miss rate a lot.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started by chris at 2026-03-18T12:50:13Z for experiment 'slo-mb-cap-and-kernel-pref'. monitoring windows active.
alex: tactical note — hedged-reads for KV could help short-term: issue a parallel KV lookup after 35ms timeout so we don't sit on a slow cache miss. that buys p99 without hurting throughput too much.
elaine: ok let's run the canary with microbatch_cap=12 + kv-prefix-normalize + kernel-pref. monitor p95/p99 for the next 30m. if p99 stabilizes near baseline we roll forward. :eyes: :thumbsup:
chris: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/562 (adds logs + mb cap flag + kernel toggle). will push canary in 2m.
samir: after the normalization patch locally, miss rate dropped to ~18% on the reproduced trace and tail latency went from 812ms -> 210ms. promising but need prod validation.
elaine: thanks team — keep updates short here, post any sudden regressions. if canary holds for 30m we promote.
